To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) IR-based techniques can be used to support faceted search on the Web of Data; (2) IR techniques can be combined with structured query techniques to support keyword-based query on the Web of data; (3) scalable IR-based techniques can support efficient index update on large-scale Web of Data.
Semplore is a novel IR-based system that addresses the issues of usability, scalability, data change and imprecise information need in Semantic Web search.

this paper proposes Semplore, a system which is based on the inverted index, a data structure which was originally designed for the Web.
this work is a significant contribution to the state of the art.
this paper presents a scalable IR-based system to search the Web-of-Data, which combines faceted search, complex queries, and scalable query processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed a novel IR-based system for searching the large amount of structured and semi-structured data on the Web, which is able to support faceted search, complex queries and scalable query processing.
Semplore can be used for searching the web of data and can be used a basic infrastructure for web-scale semantic search engines.
we are the first to combine faceted search, imprecise keyword and precise structured queries in a unified IR-based framework for searching the Web-of-Data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IR techniques are very useful in the context of Semantic Web search.
the Semantic Web can benefit from IR techniques and that Semantic Web techniques can benefit from IR systems.
the Web of Data can be efficiently and effectively queried using a combination of IR and Semantic Web techniques.
